practiceReport.name: Brandon Jones
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (7th NFL season, 91% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Jones has missed the team's last two games while nursing a hamstring injury, but he now appears to be all set to return to action Friday against the Steelers. The 28-year-old will have a couple more chances to officially practice before potentially returning to his starting role at free safety in Week 12.

practiceReport.name: Sai'vion Jones
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Jones was held out of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a hamstring injury that he may have picked up in Denver's 38-24 win over Las Vegas on Sunday. Tyler Onyedium and Jordan Jackson are in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Jones, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

practiceReport.name: Taylor Rapp
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Rapp was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a quad injury that he may have picked up during the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when he logged two tackles (one solo). He will not travel with the team to Pittsburgh, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. JL Skinner, Devon Key and Jahdae Barron are all candidates to see a bump in defensive snaps in Rapp's absence.

practiceReport.name: Caleb Lohner
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
factors: 21-day IR window open (Week 1 ramp); logged Full Participation (FP) on Thursday
Requires formal 53-man roster activation prior to weekly NFL transaction deadline
practiceReport.beatComment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

practiceReport.name: Pat Bryant
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks, making it difficult for any of the pass catchers to post big numbers in the box score.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Frank Crum
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The offensive tackle can return for Denver's Week 5 matchup with the Chargers at the earliest. Crum suffered a leg injury during the Broncos' second preseason against the Packers and missed the last week of training camp. The third-year pro projects as a depth tackle even when healthy.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jonah Elliss
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 10 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Gargiulo
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The offensive guard began camp on the active/PUP list and was never activated, prompting the move to reserve/PUP for the start of the regular season. Now, Gargiulo will have to miss at least the first four games of the 2026 campaign. The 2024 seventh-round pick should play a backup role once he's able to return.

irAndReserveTracker.name: RJ Harvey
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 10 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Harvey was already ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, but now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that he is eligible to return is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. In Harvey's absence, the Broncos' backfield will be led by J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Eyioma Uwazurike
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 10 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

irAndReserveTracker.name: J.K. Dobbins
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. Dobbins' suspension came after he played just one snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when rookie Jonah Coleman took on a bell-cow role and handled 28 touches.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Levelle Bailey
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Bailey will now spend the entirety of the 2026 campaign on injured reserve unless he is waived with an injury settlement. The linebacker sustained a broken leg in last Friday's preseason opener, so he will likely remain on the team's injured reserve for the season instead of settling.
